title: Bloomberg This Weekend 09/27/2026
title_cn: Bloomberg This Weekend 09/27/2026
summary: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi, The New York Times Finance Reporter Maureen Farrell, Cuban Deputy Foreign Minister Carlos Fernandez de Cossio, Renaissance Macro Research Head of Economics Neil Dutta, Ways and Means Committee AI Caucus Co-Chair VA Rep. Don Beyer, Puck Washington Writer Abby Livingston, and Rutgers Eagleton Institute of Politics Director Ashley Koning. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Paramount Warner Deal Tests Hollywood’s Future
title_cn: Paramount Warner Deal Tests Hollywood’s Future
summary: Bloomberg entertainment reporter Lucas Shaw is on Bloomberg This Weekend examining Paramount Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery and the challenge of turning two legacy media companies into a growing business as cable declines and streaming growth slows. Speaking with Lisa Mateo, Shaw says the merger could reshape Hollywood while raising questions about debt, further consolidation and whether streaming companies such as Netflix need new sources of growth.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Kennedy Center Musicians Find New Stages
title_cn: Kennedy Center Musicians Find New Stages
summary: Bloomberg News Washington breaking news Editor Brian K. Sullivan is on Bloomberg This Weekend discussing uncertainty surrounding the Kennedy Center’s renovation, possible demolition and the displacement of major performing arts groups. He tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that musicians and other performers are continuing at venues across the Washington region as legal disputes complicate plans for the center.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US Iran Talks Hit Familiar Sticking Points
title_cn: US Iran Talks Hit Familiar Sticking Points
summary: Bloomberg White House correspondent and national security editor Michelle Jamrisko is on Bloomberg This Weekend discussing renewed US-Iran diplomacy after indirect talks in New York failed to overcome disagreements over sanctions, the US blockade and the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Jamrisko says the two sides remain on different timelines and also examines questions surrounding Taiwan after President Donald Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Tremors From AI to Oil Boost Popular Hedge Fund Dispersion Trade
title_cn: Tremors From AI to Oil Boost Popular Hedge Fund Dispersion Trade
summary: Wild gyrations in individual stocks on a punchy cocktail of AI euphoria and fear, a tumbling bond market and geopolitical drama bode well for a long-favored trade among hedge fund managers.

title: Inflation Keeps Pressure on the Fed
title_cn: Inflation Keeps Pressure on the Fed
summary: Renaissance Macro Research economist Neil Dutta tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the US labor market has stabilized while persistent inflation could force the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at a faster pace than investors currently expect. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Dutta says rising food and energy costs risk pushing inflation expectations higher and argues inflation remains the more pressing side of the Fed’s dual mandate. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Data Center Boom Faces Wall Street Skepticism
title_cn: Data Center Boom Faces Wall Street Skepticism
summary: New York Times finance reporter Maureen Farrell tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Wall Street is growing more skeptical of the AI data center boom as rising interest rates, local opposition and permitting delays add uncertainty and costs to projects. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Farrell says trillions of dollars in financing may require tapping public markets, but investor resistance is making planned data center IPOs harder and potentially more expensive to complete.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Whiplash Jolts Stocks as Sentiment Lurches From Fear to Greed
title_cn: AI Whiplash Jolts Stocks as Sentiment Lurches From Fear to Greed
summary: Artificial intelligence could wipe us all out. Or it might just kill our unwanted subscriptions.

title: Northeast Storm Brings Wind, Rain and Flooding
title_cn: Northeast Storm Brings Wind, Rain and Flooding
summary: Bloomberg News Meteorologist Craig Allen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the slow-moving nor’easter is weakening but will continue bringing rain and flooding risks to parts of the Northeast after strong winds and coastal flooding battered the region. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Allen says New York through Boston has borne the brunt of the storm, with additional rain possible even as the strongest winds subside. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rubenstein on the Billion Dollar Sports Boom
title_cn: Rubenstein on the Billion Dollar Sports Boom
summary: Baltimore Orioles owner, Carlyle Group co-founder and host of Bloomberg's Peer to Peer Conversations David Rubenstein tells David Gura that he bought his hometown team in part to help revitalize Baltimore and says sports owners tend to prioritize winning over operating profits. Rubenstein also discusses soaring franchise valuations and his new book, Inside the Owner’s Box, which examines the business and leadership of professional sports ownership. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: IAEA Says Iran Nuclear Oversight Can Resume Fast
title_cn: IAEA Says Iran Nuclear Oversight Can Resume Fast
summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi sat down with David Gura and said that Iran retains a significant amount of uranium enriched to 60%, while inspectors have lost access needed to verify the status of nuclear material and facilities damaged by military strikes. Grossi also says inspections could resume quickly if there is political will for a new agreement, while also discussing his campaign to become the next UN secretary-general. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Rejects Iran Plan to Reopen Hormuz
title_cn: Trump Rejects Iran Plan to Reopen Hormuz
summary: Bloomberg News Middle East reporter Dan Williams and Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone are on Bloomberg This Weekend discussing President Donald Trump’s rejection of Iran’s latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart negotiations, as the conflict continues to strain global energy markets. They tell hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that economic pressure could shape the next phase of diplomacy, while rising fuel costs and shifting US supply and Chinese demand remain critical factors for oil prices. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Emerging Market Investors Shun Riskiest Bonds as US Yields Soar
title_cn: Emerging Market Investors Shun Riskiest Bonds as US Yields Soar
summary: Emerging-market investors from Aegon USA Investment Management to JPMorgan Asset Management are dialing back their riskiest bond bets as the deepening selloff in global credit markets threatens to derail a stellar run for debt in the developing world.

title: A Hockey Legend, a New Bridge, and the Trade War Tearing Neighbors Apart
title_cn: A Hockey Legend, a New Bridge, and the Trade War Tearing Neighbors Apart
summary: After 25 years of planning and eight years of construction, the Gordie Howe Bridge finally opened between Detroit and Windsor this July. But the ceremony was attended only by Canadian officials, a sign of just how much the relationship between the two countries has deteriorated. What does it mean for businesses on the ground, and what can we learn about the future of US-Canada relations? (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Barrick Mining Reaches Deal With Mali Unions, Averting Strikes
title_cn: Barrick Mining Reaches Deal With Mali Unions, Averting Strikes
summary: Barrick Mining Corp. has reached an agreement with unions representing workers at its Loulo-Gounkoto gold mining operation in western Mali, averting strikes planned to begin on Monday.

title: El Niño Could Push Up Food Prices in Southern Africa
title_cn: El Niño Could Push Up Food Prices in Southern Africa
summary: Absa AgriBusiness agricultural economist Zama Sangweni says El Niño could reduce summer crop yields and put upward pressure on food prices. She explains how more severe weather could also reshape regional trade and why countries including Zambia may be especially exposed through agriculture, employment and hydropower. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China Dispatches Pair of Pandas to Atlanta Zoo: CCTV Reports
title_cn: China Dispatches Pair of Pandas to Atlanta Zoo: CCTV Reports
summary: China’s giant pandas Pingping and Fushuang departed Chengdu for Zoo Atlanta early Sunday on a chartered flight, beginning a 10-year stay in the US, China Central Television reported on Sunday.

title: Thai PM Anutin’s Support Drops in Latest Poll as Pressures Rise
title_cn: Thai PM Anutin’s Support Drops in Latest Poll as Pressures Rise
summary: Public support for Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and his Bhumjaithai Party has plunged, according to an opinion poll, as his government confronts rising oil prices and a court ruling that may threaten its hold on power.

title: China’s Consumer Stocks Face Lost Decade as AI Steals Spotlight
title_cn: China’s Consumer Stocks Face Lost Decade as AI Steals Spotlight
summary: Under the shadow of Beijing’s single-minded focus on artificial intelligence, China’s consumer stocks are trapped in a lost decade.

title_cn: China May Let Alibaba Buy New Nvidia Chips, The Information Says
summary: The Chinese government has signaled it may allow companies such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and ByteDance Ltd to purchase Nvidia Corp.’s new RTX Pro 5500 chips, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

title: AI Safety Concerns Put Congress on the Spot
title_cn: AI Safety Concerns Put Congress on the Spot
summary: Democratic Rep. Don Beyer of Virginia tells Bloomberg This Weekend that recent AI incidents have increased the urgency for federal safeguards, including safety testing and mandatory reporting of serious problems involving advanced models. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Beyer, co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus, says Congress should create a regulatory structure that combines federal oversight with technical expertise from AI companies. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Why Humanoid Robots Might Be the Future of Elder Care
title_cn: Why Humanoid Robots Might Be the Future of Elder Care
summary: The US spends roughly $400 billion a year on long-term care, and for every 100 people over 65, only four formal caregivers exist. Humanoid robots like Abi, built by Andromeda to provide emotional companionship for dementia patients, are an early attempt to ease that pressure. Andromeda COO Jennifer Haroon, Brookings researcher Gopi Goda, 1X Chief Designer Dar Sleeper, and Nvidia's Kimberly Powell discuss whether robots can truly help solve the elder care crisis, or whether the technology still has too far to go. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Meta’s VR Glasses Are Exactly What the Apple Vision Pro Should Have Been
title_cn: Meta’s VR Glasses Are Exactly What the Apple Vision Pro Should Have Been
summary: Apple weighs what to do next with its headset.

title: Bill Gates Says Trump Is Wrong to Hold Out Against AI Safeguards
title_cn: Bill Gates Says Trump Is Wrong to Hold Out Against AI Safeguards
summary: Microsoft Corp. co-founder Bill Gates said government safeguards against potentially catastrophic artificial intelligence risks won’t hamper the US in its competition with China, contrasting with President Donald Trump’s largely hands-off approach.

title: Australia Senate Requests OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs Face AI Inquiry
title_cn: Australia Senate Requests OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs Face AI Inquiry
summary: The heads of artificial intelligence firms OpenAI and Anthropic PBC have been called on to appear before an Australian Senate inquiry to answer questions after the recent revelation of a hack of a government website.

title: China Media Says US Shares Responsibility for Managing AI
title_cn: China Media Says US Shares Responsibility for Managing AI
summary: China and the US have the ability and responsibility to manage and develop artificial intelligence, according to a post published Sunday by Yuyuantantian, a social media account affiliated with state broadcaster China Central Television.

title: How AI Is Helping African Farmers Prepare for El Niño
title_cn: How AI Is Helping African Farmers Prepare for El Niño
summary: Opportunity International's Tim Strong explains how a WhatsApp-based AI tool gives smallholder farmers locally relevant advice on what and when to plant. The technology is designed to help farmers make better decisions and reduce the cost of uncertainty as weather patterns become increasingly unpredictable. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Australia’s Deputy PM Defends Data Security After OpenAI Hack
title_cn: Australia’s Deputy PM Defends Data Security After OpenAI Hack
summary: Australia’s sensitive government data is kept in a “fortress,” Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles said Sunday, seeking to reassure the public after revelations last week that an OpenAI model hacked a government website.

title: US Policy on Taiwan Unchanged After Xi Visit, Perdue Says
title_cn: US Policy on Taiwan Unchanged After Xi Visit, Perdue Says
summary: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping discuss Taiwan arms sales every time they get together but the American stance on the self-ruled island remains unchanged following the Chinese leader’s state visit to Washington last week, the US president’s top envoy to Beijing said.

title_cn: Iran Says Won’t Soften Demands as Trump Rejects Hormuz Offer
summary: Iran stuck to its seven-day proposal for reopening the crucial Strait of Hormuz, saying it won’t soften its conditions, while President Donald Trump sent mixed signals about his willingness to reach a deal.

title_cn: Russia Hits Ukraine Data Centers in Barrage That Killed Six
summary: Russian airstrikes overnight and early Sunday killed at least six people across Ukraine and targeted a number of major data centers in Kyiv, officials said.

summary: President Donald Trump hailed as “fantastic” the arrests of five men believed to be plotting an attack on a British airbase used by the US, saying the suspects were “looking to do big damage” to the facility.

title_cn: Trump Says He Expects Renewed Iran Talks This Week, Axios Says

title: Burnham Hints at New UK Taxes to Fund Major Reform to Elder Care
title_cn: Burnham Hints at New UK Taxes to Fund Major Reform to Elder Care
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham displayed a willingness to take on one of the toughest policy traps in British policies by pledging to overhaul care for the elderly. He also indicated he may introduce new taxes to pay for it.

title: Kazakh President Fires Defense Minister After Drill Deaths
title_cn: Kazakh President Fires Defense Minister After Drill Deaths
summary: Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev dismissed his defense minister after 14 military personnel died during exercises in the Caspian Sea.

title: Midterm Fight Expands Into Republican Strongholds
title_cn: Midterm Fight Expands Into Republican Strongholds
summary: Puck News Washington writer Abby Livingston and Rutgers Eagleton Poll director Ashley Koning are on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss polling that shows Democrats gaining ground ahead of the midterms, including in traditionally Republican states and districts. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, they examine how economic concerns, farm policy and attitudes toward President Donald Trump are shaping races including the closely contested Texas Senate campaign.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Slovakia’s Fico Warns of Snap Vote as Coalition Majority at Risk
title_cn: Slovakia’s Fico Warns of Snap Vote as Coalition Majority at Risk
summary: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said elections may be held as soon as January, as infighting between members of his ruling coalition threaten to cost him a majority in parliament.

title: Burnham Faces First Labour Conference as PM
title_cn: Burnham Faces First Labour Conference as PM
summary: Bloomberg Daybreak Europe anchor Caroline Hepker is on Bloomberg This Weekend previewing Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s first Labour Party conference as leader, where his plans for social care, housing and other reforms face the constraints of a difficult UK fiscal outlook. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini from Liverpool, Hepker says Burnham has ruled out an early election as his government prepares for a challenging budget and tries to build on an initial increase in confidence. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Turkey’s Ruling-Party Deputy Chair Resigns Amid Allegations Over Fund Crisis
title_cn: Turkey’s Ruling-Party Deputy Chair Resigns Amid Allegations Over Fund Crisis
summary: Turkey’s widening fund crisis reached the ruling AK Party’s leadership, with Deputy Chair Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya stepping down from her party post after opposition allegations about stock trades involving her and her husband.

title: US China Trade Truce Leaves Key Issues Unresolved
title_cn: US China Trade Truce Leaves Key Issues Unresolved
summary: Bloomberg News Washington Bureau Chief Peggy Collins is on Bloomberg This Weekend discussing stalled US-Iran negotiations, President Donald Trump’s summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and the continuing dispute over White House press access. She tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that the US-China summit extended the trade truce through Jan. 10 but left major trade and AI questions unresolved, while political and cost-of-living pressures are intensifying ahead of the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Burnham Draws Backlash With Cool Response to Heathrow Expansion
title_cn: Burnham Draws Backlash With Cool Response to Heathrow Expansion
summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s suggestion that he could block plans for a third runway at Heathrow Airport set up a dispute with influential Labour interest groups just as the governing party’s annual conference got underway.

title_cn: China Conducts Air-Sea Exercise Near Scarborough Shoal on Sunday
summary: China‘s People’s Liberation Army Southern Theater Command conducted a joint naval and air training exercise in the waters and airspace around Scarborough Shoal on Sept. 27.

title: Malaysia’s BN Says It Will Quit Coalition at Next Election: NST
title_cn: Malaysia’s BN Says It Will Quit Coalition at Next Election: NST
summary: Malaysia’s Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said his Barisan Nasional party will leave the ruling coalition once parliament is dissolved at the next election, the New Straits Times reported.

title: Would-Be Merz Successor Chides Chancellor for Reform Stasis
title_cn: Would-Be Merz Successor Chides Chancellor for Reform Stasis
summary: A key figure in Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union criticized the German chancellor’s government over the pace of economic reforms and said delays in enacting legislation were a factor in the party’s disastrous performance in three regional elections this month.

title: Serb President Vucic to Quit in Switch to PM Post, Echoing Putin’s Power Move
title_cn: Serb President Vucic to Quit in Switch to PM Post, Echoing Putin’s Power Move
summary: Embattled Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic is expected to resign on Sunday in a well-telegraphed move as he seeks to transition to the role of prime minister as a way of staying close to power in the Balkan nation.
